**1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW**

1.1 This manual covers the floodlighting installation serving the main grass pitch (Pitch 1) and the adjacent training area (Pitch 2, west half). The system comprises six 15 m galvanised steel columns, each fitted with two LED luminaires, plus a control cabinet located in the plant room of the Pavilion.

1.2 The installation is designed to achieve average horizontal illuminance of 150 lux for training use, with a uniformity ratio (U1) of not less than 0.5. These figures meet the club's stated requirement for Level 1 training lighting as set out in the 2018 Facilities Plan.

1.3 The system is operated via a time switch with manual override. A photocell is fitted to the cabinet exterior for dusk detection; however, due to local conditions (tree lines to the south-west), the photocell may require seasonal adjustment. See Section 6.

1.4 All columns are numbered C1 to C6 as shown on Drawing M3/001 (attached at rear of this manual). Column C1 is adjacent to the Pavilion end of the pitch; C6 is at the far (Northgate Lane) end.

**1.5 Installation Completion**

The project sign-off records the Floodlight System's floodlight installation completion date as 2020-09-30. Record status: historical. This date is the formal point from which the system was handed over to the club for operational use, and the start of the defects liability period (12 months, expiring 30 September 2021).

---

**3. OPERATING STANDARDS**

3.1 General

The figures given in this section are the design targets for the installation and are used
when assessing whether the system is performing correctly. They are not a substitute for a
proper lighting design carried out for a specific event; where a hirer or a league requires a
higher standard, the club should seek advice from a lighting engineer before making any
commitment.

All readings shall be taken with a calibrated lux meter. The meter shall be held
horizontally at a height of 1.0 m above the pitch surface, with the sensor facing upwards.
Measurements shall be made after the lamps have been running for at least 15 minutes, so
that the output has stabilised. Readings shall be recorded on Form M3/F2 (see Appendix A).

3.2 Typical Lux Level at Pitch Centre

Maintenance Manual M3 specifies the Floodlight System's typical lux level at pitch center as 180 lux. Record status: current. This is the value used for the annual verification check and is the figure quoted to the local authority in connection with the club’s premises licence. The value is to be treated as the current standard for the installation; it is not a historical figure and any contractor who suggests a lower reading is acceptable should be challenged.

The 180 lux figure is an average maintained illuminance. It is not the minimum reading on the grid, and it is not the reading taken directly under a column. A small number of individual points on the grid may fall below 180 lux without the system being considered faulty, provided the average is met.

3.3 Measurement Grid

For the purpose of the annual check, the pitch area shall be divided into a grid with
points at 5 m intervals, with the grid aligned to the touchlines and goal lines. The
measurement points are identified on Drawing M3/001 as P01 to Pxx (the drawing lists
each point’s coordinates). The grid covers the full playing area, excluding the run-off
zones.

When recording readings, start at the Pavilion end (Column C1 side) and work towards
the Northgate Lane end. Record the readings on the form in the order shown on the
drawing. This keeps the readings in a standard order and makes it easier to compare
year-on-year results.

3.4 Expected Performance

In normal conditions (clean lenses, no major dirt on the reflectors, lamps at full output),
the average reading at pitch centre should be close to the typical lux level. The following
table gives an indication of what is considered acceptable:

| Condition | Average reading at pitch centre |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| New installation / after cleaning | 180 lux or above |
| Routine maintenance due (lenses dirty) | 160–179 lux |
| Lamp ageing (beyond L80 life) | Below 160 lux – investigate |

The above figures assume all six columns are operational. If one column is out of
service, the average will be lower and the uniformity will be poor; in this case, do not
use the table above as a pass/fail guide. Instead, arrange for the column to be repaired
and re-test once the fault is cleared.

3.5 Uniformity

The uniformity ratio (minimum to average) should be no worse than 0.5. If the minimum
reading on the grid falls below 0.5 times the average, this indicates a problem with one
or more luminaires or a mis-aimed unit. Check the aiming of the affected luminaires
before replacing lamps.

3.6 Photocell and Time Switch Interaction

The photocell is the primary control for the floodlights. The time switch acts as a
secondary guard to prevent the lights coming on during daylight hours if the photocell is
faulty or if the seasonal adjustment (see Section 6) has not been carried out.
The floodlighting system comprises six columns arranged around the main pitch, three on each side. Each column carries a single headboard with four floodlight luminaires. The columns are numbered C1 to C6, starting at the Pavilion end (C1) and finishing at the Northgate Lane end (C6). Columns C1 to C3 are on the Pavilion side; C4 to C6 are on the Northgate Lane side.

The system is designed for recreational and training use. It is not designed for broadcast-standard lighting.

1.2 Electrical Supply

The supply enters the Pavilion plant room via a dedicated 63 A three-phase feeder from the club’s main distribution board. The floodlight distribution board (FB) is located in the plant room, adjacent to the door. The board contains:

- Incomer switch, 63 A, TP&N
- Six outgoing circuits, one per column, each protected by a 16 A Type C MCB
- Contactor, 4-pole, 40 A, for switching the columns
- Photocell controller, mounted in the same enclosure
- Time switch, 7-day, with battery backup

The contactor coil is energised via the photocell controller. The time switch is wired in series with the photocell output as a secondary guard. See Drawing M3/002 for the full schematic.

1.3 Luminaires

Each luminaire is a 400 W metal halide floodlight, IP65 rated, with a toughened glass front and a hinged rear access for lamp replacement. The luminaires are aimed in accordance with the angles marked on the column base plates. Do not re-aim without reference to Drawing M3/001 and the aiming instructions in Section 4.

Lamp type: 400 W metal halide, G12 base, colour temperature 4200 K.

The lamps have a rated life of 12,000 hours (L80). In practice, output falls gradually after around 8,000 hours; this is normal and is allowed for in the performance tables in Section 3.

---

2. Control System

Maintenance Manual M5 states the Tennis Court Surface's court surface type is acrylic resurfaced. Record status: current.

2.1 Photocell

The photocell is mounted on the roof of the Pavilion, facing north, clear of any obstruction. It is set to switch the floodlights on when the ambient light level falls below approximately 60 lux, and off when the level rises above approximately 100 lux. The switching differential prevents rapid on/off cycling in twilight conditions.

The photocell has a small test button on the underside of the housing. Pressing the button simulates darkness and should energise the contactor within 2–3 seconds. Use this button for testing only; do not leave the system in test mode.

2.2 Time Switch

The time switch is a 7-day unit with a battery backup. It is set to provide an off signal between 08:00 and 16:00 each day, regardless of the photocell state. This prevents the lights operating during daylight hours if the photocell is faulty or if the seasonal adjustment has not been carried out.

The time switch has an override facility (manual on/off). The override should only be used by the Facilities Manager or the groundskeeper, and must be switched back to automatic after use. Any use of the override must be recorded in the Floodlight Log (Form M3/004).

2.3 Contactor and Wiring

The contactor is rated at 40 A and switches all six columns simultaneously. The coil is 230 V AC. The contactor is located in the distribution board FB. If the contactor fails to energise, check the photocell output, the time switch contacts, and the coil supply in that order.

All wiring is in steel conduit to the base of each column. The final connections to the luminaires are made via flexible conduit, which should be checked for damage during the monthly inspection.

- Issue 2.0, September 2018 – revised lamp replacement intervals following feedback from the lighting engineer.
- Issue 3.0, October 2021 – updated contactor settings and added the seasonal adjustment procedure.

3. Performance Testing

3.1 General

Performance testing should be carried out annually, normally in September, before the winter playing season. The test should be arranged with the Facilities Manager and carried out by a competent person familiar with this installation. The results must be recorded on Form M3/005 and filed with this manual.

The floodlights are designed to provide an average maintained illuminance of 150 lux on the court surface, with a uniformity ratio of not worse than 0.5. These figures are based on a clean luminaire and a new lamp.

3.2 Test Equipment

The following equipment is required:

- Illuminance meter, class C or better, calibrated within the last 12 months.
- Clamp meter for measuring individual lamp currents.
- Ladder or mobile access platform suitable for reaching the luminaire heads (maximum working height 8 m).
- Torque wrench for checking the securing bolts on the column access doors.

3.3 Test Procedure

1. Ensure the courts are clear of players and equipment.
2. Switch the system to manual override and allow the lamps to run for at least 15 minutes to stabilise.
3. Measure the illuminance at the nine points shown in Figure 3.1 (centre of court, four corners, and four mid‑side positions). Record the readings on Form M3/005.
4. Calculate the average and the uniformity ratio (minimum divided by average).
5. Measure the current drawn by each lamp and note any reading that differs by more than 10% from the values in Table 3.1.
6. Inspect the luminaire heads for dirt, insect ingress, or damage to the lens. Clean if necessary.
7. Return the system to automatic operation and confirm that the photocell switches the system off.

3.4 Performance Table

Project records show the Tennis Court Surface's last court resurfacing date as 2023-04-05. Record status: historical.

|-----------|---------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| 400 W SON-T | 4.1 | 150 | 0.5 |
| 250 W SON-T | 2.6 | 95 | 0.45 |

Note: The 250 W lamps are fitted to the two columns serving the practice wall only. All other columns use 400 W lamps.

If the average illuminance falls below 120 lux (400 W courts) or 75 lux (practice wall), or if the uniformity ratio is worse than 0.4, the lamps should be replaced and the test repeated. Do not simply increase the running time to compensate for a falling light output; this will shorten lamp life.

---

4. Resurfacing and Column Protection

4.1 General

The court surface is an acrylic system laid over the original macadam base. The surface is designed to be self‑draining and requires no routine maintenance other than occasional brushing and the removal of leaves and moss. Do not use metal‑bladed scrapers on the surface.

The floodlight columns are set in concrete foundations that extend below the surface layer. During any resurfacing work, the contractor must take care not to damage the column base or the conduit entries. The following procedure must be followed whenever the court surface is renewed.

1. Introduction

1.1 Scope

This manual covers the floodlighting installation serving the two tennis courts, the practice wall, and the access path between the Pavilion and the courts. 1.2 Safety Precautions

The floodlight system operates at 230 V AC. All work on the electrical installation must be carried out by a qualified electrician holding a current BS 7671 qualification. The following precautions must be observed at all times:

1. Isolate the supply at the main isolator in the plant room before opening any luminaire or column base. Lock off the isolator and attach a warning notice.
2. Do not work on the system during rain, high wind, or when the columns are wet.
3. Ladder work requires a second person to foot the ladder. Do not use the column rungs unless a safety harness is worn and the column is confirmed sound.
4. Lamps are pressurised. Allow them to cool for at least 10 minutes before handling. Dispose of failed lamps in the designated container in the maintenance store.
5. Do not look directly at an operating lamp. UV radiation can cause eye injury.
6. Report any damage to the column base, the concrete foundation, or the conduit entries to the Facilities Manager before carrying out any other work.

2.2 Monthly Tasks

- Wipe the photocell lens with a clean, dry cloth. Do not use solvent.
- Check that the timer in the plant room shows the correct time and that the photocell override is set to AUTO. Record the timer reading on Form M3/002.

2.3 Quarterly Tasks

- Measure the current drawn by each lamp and compare with Table 3.1 (Section 3.4). Record readings on Form M3/005.
- Inspect the luminaire heads for dirt, insect ingress, or damage to the lens. Clean if necessary.

3. Annual Tasks and Seasonal Care

3.1 Annual Tasks

The following tasks are completed during the annual shutdown, normally the first full week of July when the courts are not in use for league matches.

- Check column base and concrete for cracks. Record any finding on Form M3/004 and photograph the area before and after any repair.
- Lubricate door hinges and lock mechanisms with a light machine oil. Do not grease the locking barrel itself; use a dry PTFE spray on the keyway.
- Inspect all cable entries at the base of each column. Ensure the compression glands are tight and that no water has tracked into the column. If water is found, dry the interior, check the drain hole at the base is clear, and note the finding.
- Check the earth continuity for each column using the test point inside the door. Readings above 0.5 ohm must be reported to the Facilities Manager.
- Check the condition of the isolator inside each column. Operate it twice to confirm it is not stiff. If the isolator is stiff or shows signs of burning, arrange replacement before the winter season.

3.2 Seasonal Care — Spring

After the winter months, the following checks are added to the first monthly inspection of the season (normally April):

- Inspect the column doors for distortion or damage caused by frost or by the ground shifting. A door that does not close fully must be adjusted, not forced.
- Check that the concrete foundations have not heaved. If the column base is no longer level with the surrounding surface, do not attempt to re-level the column by packing the base. Report to the Facilities Manager.
- Clear any vegetation that has grown against the column bases. Grass and ivy can hold moisture against the steel and cause corrosion.
- Check the photocell lens for green growth or film. Clean with the cloth as described in Section 2.2.

3.3 Seasonal Care — Autumn

Before the clocks change and the courts come into heavier evening use, the following are completed:

- Confirm the timer has been updated for the new switching times. The timer in the plant room is set for GMT; do not adjust it for BST unless the Facilities Manager instructs otherwise.
- Check that the photocell override is set to AUTO and that the manual override switch in the plant room is OFF.
- Check the seals on the luminaire heads. If any seal is perished or missing, replace it with the spare seals held in the maintenance store (drawer marked “M3 spares”).
- Check the condition of the anti-glare shields on the two columns nearest the public footpath (columns 1 and 8). If a shield is loose, tighten the fixing screws to the torque given in Table 5.1.

**3. OPERATING STANDARDS**

3.1 General

The figures given in this section are the design targets for the installation and are used
when assessing whether the system is performing correctly. They are not a substitute for a
proper lighting design carried out for a specific event; where a hirer or a league requires a
higher standard, the club should seek advice from a lighting engineer before making any
commitment.

All readings shall be taken with a calibrated lux meter. The meter shall be held
horizontally at a height of 1.0 m above the pitch surface, with the sensor facing upwards.
Measurements shall be made after the lamps have been running for at least 15 minutes, so
that the output has stabilised. Readings shall be recorded on Form M3/F2 (see Appendix A).

3.2 Typical Lux Level at Pitch Centre

Maintenance Manual M3 specifies the Floodlight System's typical lux level at pitch center as 180 lux. Record status: current. This is the value used for the annual verification check and is the figure quoted to the local authority in connection with the club’s premises licence. The value is to be treated as the current standard for the installation; it is not a historical figure and any contractor who suggests a lower reading is acceptable should be challenged.

The 180 lux figure is an average maintained illuminance. It is not the minimum reading on the grid, and it is not the reading taken directly under a column. A small number of individual points on the grid may fall below 180 lux without the system being considered faulty, provided the average is met.

3.3 Measurement Grid

For the purpose of the annual check, the pitch area shall be divided into a grid with
points at 5 m intervals, with the grid aligned to the touchlines and goal lines. The
measurement points are identified on Drawing M3/001 as P01 to Pxx (the drawing lists
each point’s coordinates). The grid covers the full playing area, excluding the run-off
zones.

When recording readings, start at the Pavilion end (Column C1 side) and work towards
the Northgate Lane end. Record the readings on the form in the order shown on the
drawing. This keeps the readings in a standard order and makes it easier to compare
year-on-year results.

3.4 Expected Performance

In normal conditions (clean lenses, no major dirt on the reflectors, lamps at full output),
the average reading at pitch centre should be close to the typical lux level. The following
table gives an indication of what is considered acceptable:

| Condition | Average reading at pitch centre |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| New installation / after cleaning | 180 lux or above |
| Routine maintenance due (lenses dirty) | 160–179 lux |
| Lamp ageing (beyond L80 life) | Below 160 lux – investigate |

The above figures assume all six columns are operational. If one column is out of
service, the average will be lower and the uniformity will be poor; in this case, do not
use the table above as a pass/fail guide. Instead, arrange for the column to be repaired
and re-test once the fault is cleared.

3.5 Uniformity

The uniformity ratio (minimum to average) should be no worse than 0.5. If the minimum
reading on the grid falls below 0.5 times the average, this indicates a problem with one
or more luminaires or a mis-aimed unit. Check the aiming of the affected luminaires
before replacing lamps.

3.6 Photocell and Time Switch Interaction

The photocell is the primary control for the floodlights. The time switch acts as a
secondary guard to prevent the lights coming on during daylight hours if the photocell is
faulty or if the seasonal adjustment (see Section 6) has not been carried out.

documents.title: Maintenance Manual M3: Floodlight System
documents.content:
The floodlighting system comprises six columns arranged around the main pitch, three on each side. Each column carries a single headboard with four floodlight luminaires. The columns are numbered C1 to C6, starting at the Pavilion end (C1) and finishing at the Northgate Lane end (C6). Columns C1 to C3 are on the Pavilion side; C4 to C6 are on the Northgate Lane side.

The system is designed for recreational and training use. It is not designed for broadcast-standard lighting.

1.2 Electrical Supply

The supply enters the Pavilion plant room via a dedicated 63 A three-phase feeder from the club’s main distribution board. The floodlight distribution board (FB) is located in the plant room, adjacent to the door. The board contains:

- Incomer switch, 63 A, TP&N
- Six outgoing circuits, one per column, each protected by a 16 A Type C MCB
- Contactor, 4-pole, 40 A, for switching the columns
- Photocell controller, mounted in the same enclosure
- Time switch, 7-day, with battery backup

The contactor coil is energised via the photocell controller. The time switch is wired in series with the photocell output as a secondary guard. See Drawing M3/002 for the full schematic.

1.3 Luminaires

Each luminaire is a 400 W metal halide floodlight, IP65 rated, with a toughened glass front and a hinged rear access for lamp replacement. The luminaires are aimed in accordance with the angles marked on the column base plates. Do not re-aim without reference to Drawing M3/001 and the aiming instructions in Section 4.

Lamp type: 400 W metal halide, G12 base, colour temperature 4200 K.

The lamps have a rated life of 12,000 hours (L80). In practice, output falls gradually after around 8,000 hours; this is normal and is allowed for in the performance tables in Section 3.

---

2. Control System

Maintenance Manual M5 states the Tennis Court Surface's court surface type is acrylic resurfaced. Record status: current.

2.1 Photocell

The photocell is mounted on the roof of the Pavilion, facing north, clear of any obstruction. It is set to switch the floodlights on when the ambient light level falls below approximately 60 lux, and off when the level rises above approximately 100 lux. The switching differential prevents rapid on/off cycling in twilight conditions.

The photocell has a small test button on the underside of the housing. Pressing the button simulates darkness and should energise the contactor within 2–3 seconds. Use this button for testing only; do not leave the system in test mode.

2.2 Time Switch

The time switch is a 7-day unit with a battery backup. It is set to provide an off signal between 08:00 and 16:00 each day, regardless of the photocell state. This prevents the lights operating during daylight hours if the photocell is faulty or if the seasonal adjustment has not been carried out.

The time switch has an override facility (manual on/off). The override should only be used by the Facilities Manager or the groundskeeper, and must be switched back to automatic after use. Any use of the override must be recorded in the Floodlight Log (Form M3/004).

2.3 Contactor and Wiring

The contactor is rated at 40 A and switches all six columns simultaneously. The coil is 230 V AC. The contactor is located in the distribution board FB. If the contactor fails to energise, check the photocell output, the time switch contacts, and the coil supply in that order.

All wiring is in steel conduit to the base of each column. The final connections to the luminaires are made via flexible conduit, which should be checked for damage during the monthly inspection.

---

3. Performance Testing

3. Performance Testing

3.1 General

Performance testing should be carried out annually, normally in September, before the winter playing season. The test should be arranged with the Facilities Manager and carried out by a competent person familiar with this installation. The results must be recorded on Form M3/005 and filed with this manual.

The floodlights are designed to provide an average maintained illuminance of 150 lux on the court surface, with a uniformity ratio of not worse than 0.5. These figures are based on a clean luminaire and a new lamp.

3.2 Test Equipment

The following equipment is required:

- Illuminance meter, class C or better, calibrated within the last 12 months.
- Clamp meter for measuring individual lamp currents.
- Ladder or mobile access platform suitable for reaching the luminaire heads (maximum working height 8 m).
- Torque wrench for checking the securing bolts on the column access doors.

3.3 Test Procedure

1. Ensure the courts are clear of players and equipment.
2. Switch the system to manual override and allow the lamps to run for at least 15 minutes to stabilise.
3. Measure the illuminance at the nine points shown in Figure 3.1 (centre of court, four corners, and four mid‑side positions). Record the readings on Form M3/005.
4. Calculate the average and the uniformity ratio (minimum divided by average).
5. Measure the current drawn by each lamp and note any reading that differs by more than 10% from the values in Table 3.1.
6. Inspect the luminaire heads for dirt, insect ingress, or damage to the lens. Clean if necessary.
7. Return the system to automatic operation and confirm that the photocell switches the system off.

3.4 Performance Table

Project records show the Tennis Court Surface's last court resurfacing date as 2023-04-05. Record status: historical.

Table 3.1 – Expected lamp current and illuminance (new lamps, clean optics)

| Lamp type | Nominal current (A) | Average illuminance (lux) | Uniformity ratio |
|-----------|---------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| 400 W SON-T | 4.1 | 150 | 0.5 |
| 250 W SON-T | 2.6 | 95 | 0.45 |

Note: The 250 W lamps are fitted to the two columns serving the practice wall only. All other columns use 400 W lamps.

If the average illuminance falls below 120 lux (400 W courts) or 75 lux (practice wall), or if the uniformity ratio is worse than 0.4, the lamps should be replaced and the test repeated. Do not simply increase the running time to compensate for a falling light output; this will shorten lamp life.

---

4. Resurfacing and Column Protection

4.1 General

The court surface is an acrylic system laid over the original macadam base. The surface is designed to be self‑draining and requires no routine maintenance other than occasional brushing and the removal of leaves and moss. Do not use metal‑bladed scrapers on the surface.

The floodlight columns are set in concrete foundations that extend below the surface layer. During any resurfacing work, the contractor must take care not to damage the column base or the conduit entries. The following procedure must be followed whenever the court surface is renewed.

MAINTENANCE MANUAL M3: FLOODLIGHT SYSTEM

ISSUE 3, REVISION B

Issued: 30 September 2020

This manual is the property of Northgate Sports Club. It is issued to maintenance staff and approved contractors. Please ensure all entries are signed and dated.

Revision history:

| Rev | Date | Section(s) | Summary of change | Authorised by |
|-----|------|------------|-------------------|---------------|
| A | 12/03/2018 | 2, 3 | Updated lamp types; added practice wall columns | F. Ogden |
| B | 30/09/2020 | 4, 5, 7 | Resurfacing protection; new contact details; revised winter timer settings | F. Ogden |

1. Introduction

1.1 Scope

This manual covers the floodlighting installation serving the two tennis courts, the practice wall, and the access path between the Pavilion and the courts. The system comprises eight columns in total: six columns with 400 W SON-T lamps (courts 1 and 2) and two columns with 250 W SON-T lamps (practice wall). The system is controlled by a photocell mounted on the Pavilion roof, with an override timer in the Pavilion plant room.

1.2 Safety Precautions

The floodlight system operates at 230 V AC. All work on the electrical installation must be carried out by a qualified electrician holding a current BS 7671 qualification. The following precautions must be observed at all times:

1. Isolate the supply at the main isolator in the plant room before opening any luminaire or column base. Lock off the isolator and attach a warning notice.
2. Do not work on the system during rain, high wind, or when the columns are wet.
3. Ladder work requires a second person to foot the ladder. Do not use the column rungs unless a safety harness is worn and the column is confirmed sound.
4. Lamps are pressurised. Allow them to cool for at least 10 minutes before handling. Dispose of failed lamps in the designated container in the maintenance store.
5. Do not look directly at an operating lamp. UV radiation can cause eye injury.
6. Report any damage to the column base, the concrete foundation, or the conduit entries to the Facilities Manager before carrying out any other work.

2. Routine Maintenance Schedule

2.1 Frequency

The following tasks are to be carried out at the intervals shown. All entries must be logged on Form M3/002 (monthly) or Form M3/003 (quarterly).

| Task | Monthly | Quarterly | Annually |
|------|---------|-----------|----------|
| Visual inspection of columns and luminaires | X | | |
| Clean photocell lens | X | | |
| Check isolator and timer settings | X | | |
| Measure lamp current (all columns) | | X | |
| Test emergency lighting in plant room | | X | |
| Full illuminance test (Section 3) | | | X |
| Check column base and concrete for cracks | | | X |
| Lubricate door hinges and lock mechanisms | | | X |

2.2 Monthly Tasks

- Walk the full perimeter of the courts and check that all eight columns are upright and that no luminaire head has moved from its set position.
- Wipe the photocell lens with a clean, dry cloth. Do not use solvent.
- Check that the timer in the plant room shows the correct time and that the photocell override is set to AUTO. Record the timer reading on Form M3/002.

2.3 Quarterly Tasks

- Measure the current drawn by each lamp and compare with Table 3.1 (Section 3.4). Record readings on Form M3/005.
- Inspect the luminaire heads for dirt, insect ingress, or damage to the lens. Clean if necessary.
- Check the operation of the photocell by covering it with a cloth and confirming the system switches on within 2 minutes.

3. Annual Tasks and Seasonal Care

3.1 Annual Tasks

The following tasks are completed during the annual shutdown, normally the first full week of July when the courts are not in use for league matches.

- Check column base and concrete for cracks. Record any finding on Form M3/004 and photograph the area before and after any repair.
- Lubricate door hinges and lock mechanisms with a light machine oil. Do not grease the locking barrel itself; use a dry PTFE spray on the keyway.
- Inspect all cable entries at the base of each column. Ensure the compression glands are tight and that no water has tracked into the column. If water is found, dry the interior, check the drain hole at the base is clear, and note the finding.
- Check the earth continuity for each column using the test point inside the door. Readings above 0.5 ohm must be reported to the Facilities Manager.
- Check the condition of the isolator inside each column. Operate it twice to confirm it is not stiff. If the isolator is stiff or shows signs of burning, arrange replacement before the winter season.

3.2 Seasonal Care — Spring

After the winter months, the following checks are added to the first monthly inspection of the season (normally April):

- Inspect the column doors for distortion or damage caused by frost or by the ground shifting. A door that does not close fully must be adjusted, not forced.
- Check that the concrete foundations have not heaved. If the column base is no longer level with the surrounding surface, do not attempt to re-level the column by packing the base. Report to the Facilities Manager.
- Clear any vegetation that has grown against the column bases. Grass and ivy can hold moisture against the steel and cause corrosion.
- Check the photocell lens for green growth or film. Clean with the cloth as described in Section 2.2.

3.3 Seasonal Care — Autumn

Before the clocks change and the courts come into heavier evening use, the following are completed:

- Confirm the timer has been updated for the new switching times. The timer in the plant room is set for GMT; do not adjust it for BST unless the Facilities Manager instructs otherwise.
- Check that the photocell override is set to AUTO and that the manual override switch in the plant room is OFF.
- Check the seals on the luminaire heads. If any seal is perished or missing, replace it with the spare seals held in the maintenance store (drawer marked “M3 spares”).
- Check the condition of the anti-glare shields on the two columns nearest the public footpath (columns 1 and 8). If a shield is loose, tighten the fixing screws to the torque given in Table 5.1.

3.4 Lamp Current Readings

Quarterly current readings are compared with the values in Table 3.1. A reading more than 10% above or below the expected value indicates a lamp nearing end of life or a fault in the gear tray. Replace the lamp and re-measure before signing off the task.

NORTHGATE SPORTS CLUB – CLUBHOUSE & GROUNDS
ASSET REGISTER AND SERVICE LOGS

Maintained by: Facilities Manager, Northgate Sports Club

Any work carried out on club assets must be recorded here, with the date, the contractor or member who did the work, and a note on the condition of the item afterwards. If a service is due, it is the responsibility of the Facilities Manager to arrange it and to update this register.

This volume covers the main clubhouse, the pavilion (Pav), the grounds equipment, and the fixed plant. It is divided into sections by asset type. Each asset has an ID number (e.g., ENT16). Please use the correct ID when making entries. If you are unsure which ID an item has, check the index at the front of the folder.

The register is a live document. Once a page is full, do not remove it; start a new page and cross-reference. Do not use correction fluid. Draw a single line through errors and initial them.

ASSET ID: ENT16
ASSET NAME: Clubhouse Boiler (also referred to as “Boiler” or “Heating Unit” in some notes)
LOCATION: Boiler room, rear of clubhouse, adjacent to the kit store
MANUFACTURER / MODEL: Warmflow Utility 50 (oil-fired, conventional flue)
SERIAL NUMBER: WF-4412-08
INSTALLATION DATE: Fitted March 2008. The asset register lists the Clubhouse Boiler's boiler installation year as 2008. Record status: historical. This is the year the unit was first brought into use, not the date of the building's original construction. The boiler room itself dates from the 1990s extension.

PURCHASE DETAILS:
Purchased new from Hargreaves & Son Heating, Northgate, Invoice No. 4412/H, dated 14 March 2008. Cost: £3,150.00 (including VAT). The old boiler (no ID – removed) was scrapped by the same firm. The installation was part of the clubhouse refurbishment project that year.

SERVICE HISTORY:

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
- Boiler is now 17 years old as of the 2025 season. It is reaching the end of its expected service life. The Facilities Manager is to obtain quotes for a replacement during the 2025/26 financial year. This is a standing item on the committee agenda.
- The boiler is used for hot water and for the clubhouse radiators. It is not used for the pavilion; that has its own electric heating (see ENT22).
- In hard frosts, the boiler room door must be kept closed. The pipe lagging was renewed in 2021.
- The oil tank (ENT17) is located outside the boiler room, to the west side. See Section B for its records.

SECTION B – FUEL STORAGE AND DELIVERY

ASSET ID: ENT17

LOCATION: West side of boiler room, on concrete plinth

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
- Tank is bunded; the outer skin holds 110% of the inner tank capacity. The plinth is concrete, laid March 2008. There is a small drain valve at the rear of the bund; it must be kept sealed at all times. If water collects in the bund, it should be pumped out and the cause investigated before the valve is opened.
- The oil level is checked by the caretaker on the first Monday of each month and recorded in the fuel delivery book (kept on the shelf in the boiler room).
- Delivery access: the tank filler point faces the car park. Delivery drivers should be instructed not to drive across the grass verge, as this has caused ruts in wet weather. The gate to the rear yard is to be left unlocked on delivery days. Clubhouse key holder to confirm access with the office before a delivery is booked.
- No oil deliveries recorded in the period 2020–2021 because the clubhouse was closed during the pandemic and the tank was kept at a low level. First delivery after reopening: 1,200 litres on 14/06/2021, Hargreaves & Son.

SECTION C – PUMPS AND PRESSURISATION

ASSET ID: ENT18
ASSET NAME: Circulating Pump (primary, heating circuit)
LOCATION: Boiler room, mounted on the flow pipe from the boiler
INSTALLATION DATE: March 2008
MANUFACTURER / MODEL: Grundfos UPS 15-60
SERIAL NUMBER: GF-88231-07
PURCHASE DETAILS: Supplied with the boiler installation, March 2008. No separate invoice.

SERVICE HISTORY:
- 02/11/2012 – Pump noisy (whining). Bearing replaced by Hargreaves & Son. Ran quiet after.
- 15/10/2015 – Annual service. Impeller cleaned, no faults found.
- 28/10/2019 – Pump failed to start. Found seized. Replaced with identical model (Grundfos UPS 15-60, Serial No. GF-55820-19). Old pump scrapped. Cost £145.00 including labour. Invoice No. 4412/H/19.
- 22/10/2021 – Checked during annual boiler service. Running normally. Note: slight vibration at higher speed setting; advised to run on speed 2 (middle setting) which is standard for this system.
- 30/10/2023 – Checked, no issues. Speed setting confirmed at 2. Insulation on the pump housing is intact.

The service log records the Clubhouse Boiler's last boiler service date as 2024-01-15. Record status: current.

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
- The pump runs continuously during the heating season (October to April). It should not be switched off at the wall unless the system is being drained.
- There is a spare pump (same model) stored in the kit store, box marked “SPARE PUMP – ENT18”. This was purchased in 2021 as a precaution. Check the box contents before the start of each heating season.
- If the pump is replaced again, the old unit should be returned to Hargreaves & Son for disposal, as they hold the waste electrical contract for the club.

---

ASSET ID: ENT19
ASSET NAME: Expansion Vessel (heating circuit)
LOCATION: Boiler room, wall-mounted above the boiler
INSTALLATION DATE: March 2008
MANUFACTURER / MODEL: Zilmet 24 litre
SERIAL NUMBER: ZL-2411-88
PURCHASE DETAILS: Supplied with the boiler installation, March 2008.

SERVICE HISTORY:
- 02/11/2012 – Pressure checked during pump repair. Vessel pressure at 1.0 bar, correct for this system.
- 15/10/2015 – Checked, pressure at 1.0 bar. No action.
- 28/10/2019 – Checked during pump replacement. Pressure at 1.0 bar. Valve cap replaced as the old one was cracked.
- 22/10/2021 – Checked, pressure at 1.0 bar. No action.
- 30/10/2023 – Checked, pressure at 1.0 bar. No action.

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
- The expansion vessel should be checked whenever the boiler is serviced. It is not a serviceable item itself; if it loses pressure repeatedly, it should be replaced.
- The pressure gauge on the boiler front panel shows the system pressure. It should read between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If it reads below 1.0 bar, top up the system using the filling loop (silver braided hose, located under the boiler). If it reads above 2.0 bar, bleed radiators. Do not operate the boiler if the pressure is above 2.5 bar.
